transcript:
Meeting: POC Weekly - model harmonization + emergency rollback plan
Date: 2026-10-21 15:00 PT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Rhea (Redwood SE), Sofia (Orion ML), David (Orion Platform), Alex (Product), Priya (Security)

Summary: quick results review from last week's run, narrow to three model variants, discuss pin and failover rules, draft dead-man switch / rollback drill, agree next steps.

Topics: model variants, pinning policy, canary thresholds, circuit breaker, KV/prefix caching, quantization tradeoffs, security/compliance notes, scheduling rollback dry-run.

[00:00] Maya: okay everyone, thanks for joining, we'll keep to 45 minutes, quick review of the charges from the benchmark you sent, then focus on the harmonization and the "dead man" switch plan.
[00:38] Sofia: sounds good, we've got David and Alex on for infra questions, Priya here for security.
[01:12] Liam: quick note, we re-ran the 10k query set on three variants: base-gt2 (unquantized), q4f (4-bit finance-optimized quant), and ll-fast (low-latency distilled). spreadsheet link in chat. 
[01:46] Alex: excellent. high-level what looked best?
[02:10] Rhea: ll-fast gave best p50 latency, base-gt2 highest quality on our eval prompts, q4f sits in the middle with big cost savings but occasional drop on long-form instructions.
[02:42] David: we care about 95th percentile under 512 token context since customers do long receipt parsing. did you capture that?
[03:05] Liam: yes, 95th at 512 tokens: base-gt2 ~ 420ms, q4f ~ 720ms, ll-fast ~ 310ms. note these are run on the dedicated pool with continuous batching off for parity.
[03:38] Sofia: okay those numbers help. cost delta?
[03:52] Maya: cost per 1k tokens: base-gt2 $1.20, q4f $0.42, ll-fast $0.65 (approx). we left annotation for tokenization differences in the sheet.
[04:18] Priya: on data handling, quick flag: does the pilot run with our KMS? we need to ensure key wrapping and audit logs for any logs stored.
[04:44] Liam: for the pilot we're using Redwood-managed KMS but can flip to customer KMS on dedicated/private. there was a note in the security docs about rotating keys and audit hooks.
[05:12] Priya: we need that confirmed in writing.
[05:25] Maya: we'll include a KMS playbook excerpt and the SOC2 scope in the follow-up.
[05:40] Sofia: back to models — we want to pick a primary and 2 fallbacks for the POC. suggested: primary base-gt2 (quality), fallback 1 q4f (cost), fallback 2 ll-fast (latency). thoughts?
[06:08] Liam: I actually recommended primary base-gt2 with a shadow to q4f and a canary ring to ll-fast for low-latency routes. but we should reverse if you expect heavy latency SLAs.
[06:34] David: our main route is interactive chat so p95 matters more; we'd prefer ll-fast as primary for the chat experience, but keep base-gt2 for synthesis/long-form overnight jobs.
[06:58] Alex: so split by route, not all traffic. good point.
[07:20] Maya: that leads to the harmonization idea: route-level pinning. attribution in console: route=chat -> ll-fast pinned, route=batch -> q4f pinned, route=synthesis -> base-gt2 pinned. that gives both cost and quality controls.
[07:50] Sofia: we like that. can Redwood support per-route rollouts and emergency swaps?
[08:05] Liam: yes, we have per-route model mapping and can push canary traffic percentages, plus manual rollback commands. the "dead-man switch" you're asking about is our emergency cutover plan: automatic circuit-breaker if latency or error rate exceeds thresholds, then fallback path.
[08:34] Priya: what metrics are used for the circuit-breaker? p95 latency? error spikes? user-defined?
[08:52] Rhea: it's configurable: you can choose p95, error-rate, or token inflation. typical setting we recommend is p95 > 1200ms for 2 consecutive windows or error-rate > 5% for 5 minutes triggers canary rollback.
[09:19] David: and when it triggers, what's the order of operations?
[09:28] Liam: immediate traffic split: 100% to fallback variant as defined by the route, KV cache flush options, and alerting to on-call; plus shadowing disabled. We also store last-good-model in the version gateway to allow fast re-pin.
[09:53] Maya: important to document commands: CLI + console steps. Liam will draft the step-by-step.
[10:07] Sofia: is there a way to do a dry-run? we'd like to simulate a rollback without affecting real users.
[10:22] Liam: yes, we can do a dry-run mode where the control plane simulates the switch and reports projected latency/cost impacts, plus a commit toggle to actually apply. that requires a short window to collect telemetry.
[10:43] Alex: perfect. we want to time-box it during low traffic.
[10:54] Priya: security: can the rollback commands be gated by RBAC and SSO approval? we don't want ops to be able to flip models willy-nilly.
[11:10] Rhea: yes, RBAC + approval workflows supported; you can require 2-person approvals on major route changes and record audit log entries with the user's SAML identity.
[11:33] Maya: to reduce blast radius, recommend canary steps: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with health checks at each step and automated rollback if any window fails.
[11:53] David: for the POC we'd like a tighter canary: 2% steps and longer windows. is that supported?
[12:08] Liam: supported, though it increases time to full rollover and affects capacity planning. we'll note capacity for the dedicated pool.
[12:22] Sofia: what's the recommended shadowing approach? we want quality checks without impacting latency.
[12:37] Rhea: send 10% shadow traffic to base-gt2 for chat route, capture responses for offline evaluation. we can store diffs and do automated regression alerts for nps-like metrics.
[12:55] Alex: about caching: we've seen prefix re-use, can Redwood's prefix/KV cache be shared across variants or is it variant-specific?
[13:12] Liam: good question. KV cache keys include model ID so cache is variant-specific by default. sharing cache across compatible quantized versions is possible but risky if key encodings differ. we can do a warmed cache migration during rollout.
[13:37] Sofia: that warming step needs a plan because cache miss storms can spike costs.
[13:48] Maya: noted — include warming playbook in rollback doc.
[13:56] David: speaking of cost spikes, does the circuit-breaker also consider cost per request or token burn? sometimes high tokens due to hallucinations inflate cost.
[14:13] Rhea: yes, you can set token inflation thresholds or spend per minute thresholds. we recommend a spend cap alert separate from rollback triggers.
[14:28] Priya: for compliance, we also want retention rules — retention of logs for 90 days in pilot, and ability to purge on demand.
[14:43] Liam: retention settings are configurable per customer. purge APIs exist and we can log purge events to your audit trail.
[15:00] Maya: let's walk through a concrete rollback scenario: traffic route chat pinned to ll-fast, but ll-fast sees p95 > 1200ms for two consecutive 5min windows. system triggers the canary rollback to q4f. what happens?
[15:26] Liam: first step: control plane sets traffic to the pre-defined fallback at 100% or stepwise per your policy, disabled shadowing, flush or maintain relevant KV caches as configured, and emit events to webhook. On health being stable for X minutes, control plane marks the rollback successful; if not, operator can re-pin to last-good model or escalate to human-run mitigation.
[15:55] Sofia: in that case do we keep the old model available for queries like bulk synthesis?
[16:08] Liam: yes, routing is independent; you can re-route batch jobs to the old model while chat is on fallback.
[16:20] Alex: what about traffic bursts during rollback? do you autoscale?
[16:30] Rhea: dedicated pool autoscaling will react, but since we pre-reserve capacity we suggest a buffer of 20% in pilot. otherwise latency will spike when autoscaler spins up.
[16:47] David: what's the rollback latency — how long to move 100% of traffic?
[16:56] Liam: the control plane switch is seconds; effective p95 stabilizing depends on cache warm/warm-up and autoscaler; expect a 30s control plane change, then a few minutes for metrics to settle.
[17:12] Maya: I'd like to propose a "dead-man switch" drill: we schedule a 30-minute window, intentionally trip a simulated latency fault in ll-fast, observe automated rollback, and then evaluate time-to-recovery and any cache storms.
[17:31] Sofia: agreed, that would make us comfortable. can we do the dry run on 10/29 as mentioned?
[17:40] Maya: sounds good. Liam will own the drill with Orion on-call.
[17:48] Liam: will prepare a runbook and checklist.
[17:54] David: side question: when we pin versions, can we pin to a quantized family rather than a single build? we might want to allow minor patching within a fenced version.
[18:11] Rhea: you can pin by model family + semver range, or by exact model artifact. we support version fences and auto-approval rules for security patches only if you allow it.
[18:28] Priya: we want security patches auto-approved but not any model changes.
[18:36] Maya: we'll propose a policy: auto-approve infra/security patches, require manual approval for model weight changes.
[18:47] Sofia: cool. next, the evaluation metrics: how are regressions detected during canary?
[18:55] Liam: we compute a small set of signal metrics: Rouge-ish similarity on labeled prompts, safety classifier delta, perplexity proxies, and production response time. thresholds can be tuned per route.
[19:14] Alex: do you support running evals on shadowed responses automatically?
[19:22] Rhea: yes, we can run automated eval hooks and send regression alerts if metrics degrade beyond configured thresholds.
[19:32] Sofia: one of our prompts is multi-turn invoice parsing with strict slot extraction. q4f had issues there previously. how do we gate that?
[19:45] Liam: include that prompt in the gate set; we can create a gate that fails the canary if slot F1 drops below X. gate-based rollout enforcement is supported.
[19:58] David: storage: where do shadow responses land? are they encrypted with our key?
[20:08] Liam: shadow logs stored in your tenant bucket, encrypted with your KMS when configured.
[20:18] Priya: good. please include the encryption assurance in the doc.
[20:27] Maya: okay switching back — decision time: pick primary per route and confirm fallback order. do we have consensus?
[20:40] Sofia: yes: chat -> ll-fast primary, fallback q4f, long-batch -> q4f primary, fallback base-gt2, synth -> base-gt2 primary, fallback q4f.
[21:01] Alex: agreed.
[21:06] Maya: I'll capture that in the runbook and in the route mapping config.
[21:13] Liam: we'll also add a compatibility matrix showing which KV caches can be shared and which require warming, plus expected cold-start penalty numbers.
[21:28] David: and include cost numbers for each fallback scenario.
[21:34] Rhea: will do.
[21:38] Sofia: about monitoring, can you push metrics to our Prometheus/Grafana?
[21:46] Liam: yes via metrics exporter; we can also provide pre-built dashboards.
[21:53] Priya: how fast are audit logs accessible for compliance review? we need near-real-time.
[22:01] Maya: audit events stream within seconds to your SIEM when configured.
[22:09] Alex: are there any gotchas you want us to be aware of before we run the dry‑run?
[22:17] Liam: two things: 1) warming caches is manual unless you pre-populate, 2) shared KV across quant variants can cause tokenization mismatches. we'll document mitigation.
[22:35] Sofia: noted. on the pilot scope: we want to keep the pilot to 2% of production traffic to limit blast radius. is that okay?
[22:48] Maya: yes, pilot tenancy can be limited. just share expected qps so we size the pool.
[22:57] David: we'll send QPS and 95th SLA targets.
[23:05] Maya: action items recap: Maya and Liam to run the 48h sweep and produce results, Liam will draft rollback DRILL runbook, Sofia to share queries/traces, Priya to confirm SOC2/KMS scope.
[23:23] Alex: can you also share the per-route JSON config so we can review before the dry-run?
[23:29] Rhea: yes we'll send route config and canary thresholds.
[23:36] Sofia: timeline for deliverables?
[23:41] Maya: benchmark by 10/28, runbook by 10/26, route config and security items by 10/24, dry-run on 10/29.
[23:55] David: ok good.
[24:02] Maya: any last questions?
[24:07] Priya: just confirm that RBAC approvals are enforced for rollback.
[24:12] Liam: confirmed, we'll demo it during the dry-run.
[24:18] Sofia: one micro note: can we keep a read-only view of the rollback history? helpful for post-mortem.
[24:25] Rhea: yes historical events are preserved for 365 days by default in the console and can be exported.
[24:34] Alex: perfect.
[24:39] Maya: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and runbook links, and set the dry-run calendar invite.
[24:49] Liam: I'll include command snippets for the CLI rollback and the console screenshots.
[24:58] Sophia: thanks — (mis‑pronounced) Sofia: thanks everyone.
[25:05] [END OF TRANSCRIPT]

Notes: transcript contains occasional transcription errors (names, product tokens). Shared artifacts: https://redwood.example.com/spreadsheets/pilot-orion-2026-10 (benchmark sheet), https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/orion-rollback-dryrun (runbook draft).
